players.product: Power-first greenfield AI data-center campuses on 15-year triple-net leases (River Bend LA for Anthropic; Beacon Point TX) - ex-Bitcoin-mining platform (American Bitcoin affiliate)

quarterly_data.signal: Together with RiverBend, total contracted AI data center capacity is about 949 MW, representing roughly $26.6 billion of expected aggregate base term contract value, all produced by the same operating model in less than a year. We have three 15-year leases with investment-grade anchored counterparties in the last nine months alone.
quarterly_data.figure: ~949 MW contracted AI data-center capacity; ~$26.6B aggregate base-term contract value; three 15-year leases

capex.metric: aggregate base-term contract value across River Bend + Beacon Point (3 leases)

quarterly_data.signal: The second Beacon Point lease is for 352 MW of IT capacity and represents about $9.8 billion of expected base term contract value. An existing customer chose to expand under the same commercial framework - the customer chose to double its footprint at Beacon Point. Beacon Point now represents 704 MW of contracted IT capacity, roughly about $19.6 billion of expected base term contract value, with the campus fully commercialized with a full gigawatt of utility capacity.
quarterly_data.figure: Beacon Point Building Two: 352 MW / ~$9.8B; campus total 704 MW / ~$19.6B

quarterly_data.signal: Project financing: RiverBend $3.25 billion of fully amortizing senior secured notes due 2042, rated investment grade, non-recourse to Hut 8. Beacon Point consisted of $4.25 billion of senior secured notes, rated one notch higher above RiverBend, priced 20 points inside of RiverBend, amortization pushed from two years to four years. Together, RiverBend and Beacon Point Building One represents approximately $7.5 billion of investment-grade capital raised for construction stage development.
quarterly_data.figure: $3.25B River Bend notes + $4.25B Beacon Point notes = ~$7.5B investment-grade project debt

quarterly_data.signal: The development pipeline now stands at about 8.7 GW, up approximately 300 MW from last quarter. We have 11 sites in the under diligence and under exclusivity stages, averaging more than 650 MW each. The exclusivity stage increased by 200 MW. The reported number excludes M&A opportunities, behind the meter power generation solutions, and potential RiverBend expansion, where the tenant holds a right of first offer on the next gigawatt.
quarterly_data.figure: ~8.7 GW development pipeline (+~300 MW QoQ); 11 sites averaging >650 MW; River Bend tenant ROFO on next 1 GW

quarterly_data.signal: Revenue increased approximately 81% year-over-year to $74.9 million, while cost of revenue increased by approximately 23%. Gross profit of approximately $48 million and gross margin approximately 64%, compared with approximately 47% in the prior year period. Adjusted EBITDA, excluding digital asset mark-to-market movements, was $10.4 million vs $4.2 million. Compute revenue $72.5 million (Bitcoin mined ~935 vs ~308); digital infrastructure revenue $1.3 million - its financial profile changes materially as Riverbend and Beacon Point data halls are delivered.
quarterly_data.figure: Revenue $74.9M (+81% YoY); gross margin ~64%; adj. EBITDA $10.4M; digital infrastructure revenue only $1.3M pre-delivery

quarterly_data.signal: River Bend construction: structural steel erection began in early June; building foundations expected to be completed before month's end; steel erection on the substation began in mid-July; slab-on-grade pours beginning across the auxiliary support yard and the main building. Building one gets built really across 2027 - each data hall gets handed over; end of 2027 building two capacity has the opportunity to come online. Delivering River Bend and Beacon Point on time is our number one priority.
quarterly_data.figure: River Bend Building 1 data halls handed over across 2027; Building 2 capacity opportunity end of 2027

quarterly_data.signal: Procurement: the first Building 1 on each campus are fully contracted. 100% of long lead time bindings are contracted. GC subcontractors pricing is fixed, and that aligns with the financings that we've done. Building 2 was cheaper than Building 1. Now, as we're finalizing Building 3, we expect it to be cheaper than Building 2. We actually haven't seen a big impact when it comes to lead times, capacity and allocation and queues - we focus on building partnerships, integrating vendors' equipment into a skidded design.
quarterly_data.figure: 100% of long-lead equipment contracted for Building 1 at each campus; cost per building falling B1 -> B2 -> B3

quarterly_data.signal: If we think about roughly $27 billion of contracted revenue, that's about $1.7 billion per year of cash flow that comes in. Because these are triple net leases, all the costs in running those facilities are actually passed through to the tenant - that's why we showed kind of a 99% NOI margin. Really your cost on that capital is just servicing principal and interest on the bonds.
quarterly_data.figure: ~$27B contracted revenue = ~$1.7B per year cash flow; ~99% NOI margin (triple-net)

quarterly_data.signal: Balance sheet: approximately $233.6 million of unrestricted cash and approximately $6.8 billion of restricted cash (River Bend and Beacon Point project accounts); approximately $7.6 billion carrying amount of debt, the majority being the $3.25 billion Riverbend notes and the $4.25 billion Beacon Point notes at bankruptcy-remote project subsidiaries, non-recourse to the parent. Coinbase converted approximately $159.3 million of its note, eliminating our only remaining parent recourse debt; $200 million FalconX term loan collateralized by Bitcoin (coupon 9%-7%). Approximately 700 MW of our infrastructure supports our affiliated tenant, American Bitcoin (roughly 54% owned).
quarterly_data.figure: $233.6M unrestricted cash; ~$6.8B restricted project cash; ~$7.6B debt (non-recourse project notes); ~700 MW hosting American Bitcoin

quarterly_data.signal: On hyperscaler capex concerns: Demand is robust from all the conversations we've had. Demand is real. Demand is there. Everyone wants capacity yesterday. Every tenant will ebb and flow - some will pause for a month or two, then it turns back up. Behind-the-meter capacity will happen; at Riverbend the gas is there, plenty of access on the pipelines, and we're working with Entergy around capacity - some behind-the-meter generation working in concert with Entergy grid-connected capacity.

connects_to.relationship: River Bend (Louisiana) greenfield AI data-center campus built and leased to Anthropic on a 15-year triple-net lease; tenant holds a right of first offer on the next gigawatt

contracts.signal: Asked about Hut 8's gigawatt diligence agreement with Anthropic: 'Anthropic is a great example of a customer that needs a lot of demand and capacity to fulfill their needs. We work very closely with them, have a good relation with them. Obviously, we're building the campus in Riverbend for them. Overall, look to continue to do work and expand with them as well... have some kind of down the fairway opportunities that we're in discussions with them and have some more novel, fun opportunities.' River Bend was commercialized with an investment-grade anchor counterparty (announced last December) and financed with $3.25 billion of fully amortizing senior secured notes due 2042 covering the expected construction period and the entire 15-year lease.
contracts.units: River Bend Building 1 - ~245 MW (computed: 949 MW total contracted less 704 MW at Beacon Point); ROFO on the next gigawatt
contracts.value: ~$7.0B base-term contract value (computed: $26.6B total less $19.6B Beacon Point); $3.25B project notes fund the build
